To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the use of a lexicon liberates sufficient cognitive resources for the emergence of SVO word orders, and 2. the availability of SVO word-order is not a sufficient condition to explain the emergence of SVA (Subject-Verb-Object) syntax.
“The use of a stable lexicon liberates the cognitive resources needed to use the more efficient SVO syntax.”

(1) SVO is the most frequent word order among the world's human languages, (2) the preference for SVA word orders is triggered by the availability of a shared lexicon and (3) the preference for SOV is triggered by the need to express the syntactic relations between elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of a gesture lexicon in triggering the use of SVA, the most efficient word order in terms of information transmission.
the role of the lexicon in shaping word order preferences.
the role of a shared lexicon in the emergence of word order preferences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SVO is the most efficient word order, and that SOV is the “default” word order in human languages.
the use of a SVO order is the result of a complex interplay between the cognitive and the communicative aspects of human language.
SVO is the default word order for human languages, but that the use of SOV is triggered by the absence of a shared lexicon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a lexicon is a trigger for the emergence of SVO word orders.
the availability of a shared lexicon triggers the emergence of SVO, the most efficient word order for the expression of syntactic relations, in improvised communication.
the availability of a shared lexicon, which reduces the cognitive load, triggers the use of the more efficient word orders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of S/V word orders is a function of the amount of resources that are available to express the syntactic relations of the sentence.
the availability of a shared lexicon triggers the preference for SVA word order.
the availability of a shared lexicon triggers the emergence of SVO word orders.
